candidate_windows.window_text: In this section,we introduce PBI-Attack,a bimodal adversarial multi-round black-box jailbreak attack for LVLMs,with pipeline shown in Figure 2. Our approach is composed of two stages as shown in Algorithm 1. In the first stage, we extract malicious features from a harmful corpus and generate an adversarial image with highly harmful information injected. In the second stage,we further enhance malicious feature injection for both image and text prompt through an iterative bimodal adversarial optimization process.

Datasets. We use the same harmful content corpus to optimize benign images,following previous work(Qi et al., 2024). Additionally, we supplement our study with experiments on the HEADS dataset (Li et al.， 2024b). Our testset are 520 prompts from AdvBench (Zou et al., 2023). Models. We use MiniGPT-4(Vicuna-13B) (Zhu et al.，2023)，InstructBLIP（Vicuna-13B）(Dai et al., 2023),and LLaVA (LLaMA-2-13B) (Liu et al.，2024b) in white-box setting and Gemini (Team et al., 2023), GPT-4 (Achiam et al., 2023), and Qwen-VL (Bai et al., 2023) in black-box. Baselines. Current jailbreak attacks against LVLMs typically rely on prompt engineering, focus on unimodal optimization,and exhibit limited transferability to black-box models. We empirically compare PBI-Attack to the following SOTA methods using their reported optimal settings. · Arondight (Liu et al., 2024c) randomly combines images and texts for attacks,with the textual prompts being generated through reinforcement learning. · GCG (Zou et al., 2023) first pinpoints potential replacements for each token and chooses the one that leads to greatest loss decrease. · Advimage (Qi et al., 2024) uses a single adversarial image to jailbreak a LLM. · ImgJP (Niu et al., 2024) proposes a maximum likelihood-based algorithm to find an image jailbreaking prompt. · UMK (Wang et al., 2024b) optimizes a text suffix based on an adversarial image, using dual-modal adversarial input for jailbreak. · InPieces (Shayegani et al., 2023a) proposes four malicious text triggers and embeds them in benign images for jailbreak. · BAP (Ying et al.， 2024） employs queryagnostic image perturbing and intent-specific textual optimization. · MLAI (Hao et al., 2024) leverages scenarioaware image generation， flat-minima adversarial selection,and collaborative multiimage attacks for optimal effectiveness. · FigStep(Gong et al., 2023） turns forbidden instructions into typographic images to bypass visual safety alignment. · HADES (Li et al.,2025b) embeds and amplifies malicious intent in text via meticulously crafted images to bypass safety filters. Metrics. Toxicity assessment in optimization are based on Perspective API 1 and Detoxify classifier² (Hanu and Unitary team,2020). We use 8 attributes from Perspective API(toxicity, severe toxicity, identity attack, insult, profanity, threat, sexually explicit and flirtation,with detailed description in Appendix A） and 6 attributes in Detoxify classifier (toxicity，severe toxicity, obscene, threat, insult, identity attack). We use two metrics following Qi et al. (2024). (1) Attack Success Rate (ASR) is the proportion of instructions that result in successful jailbreaks assessed by HarmBench (Mazeika et al., 2024) with GPT-3.5-turbo³. (2) Toxicity Rate is the proportion of outputs with a toxicity score exceeding 0.5 for each toxic attribute assessed by Perspective API and Detoxify classifier. We aggregate the toxicity scores across all attributes to assess the toxicity of a response in optimization, denoted as $\mathrm { T } ( \mathbf { x } _ { \mathrm { a d v } } , \mathbf { y } _ { \mathrm { a d v } } )$ · Responses from LVLMs exhibit high randomness,with identical inputs potentially yielding vastly different outputs,posing a challenge for evaluation. Our optimization is based on response toxicity, which necessitates multiple queries and corresponding responses to reduce randomness. Specifically, we query the target model ten times for each pair of adversarial inputs and use the mean toxicity score of the responses. For each experiment, we repeat three times and report the means and standard deviations. Implementation details. All experiments are conducted on 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs with 80GB memory. We follow the configuration from previous work (Qi et al., 2024), with step size $\alpha$ of 1, batch size $^ b$ of 8,and $\lambda$ in $\mathcal { L } ( \mathbf { x } _ { \mathrm { a d v } } ^ { t } )$ is 1.0. We set the adversarial text suffix length to 1O tokens and the number of candidates to 4Oo.For each round of attack,we update either the image or the text five times per iteration, and then query the model with the current image or text. The number of queries is provided in the ablation study. And we use an iteration count of 4Oo for image optimization and 1Oo for text optimization.
